assessments.closureRisk: Low — self-contained, no external gating; closure depends only on executing the variant design and probe re-runs.
assessments.dominantCost: Designing materially different variants that are genuinely perturbed (not trivially re-skinned) and re-running causal probes across them.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Create 2-3 materially different bounded encounter variants, re-run causal-episode probes across variants, and classify surviving priors.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: AF002 priors are partially fixed-encounter overfit; perturbation across materially different Scenario/Genesis variants will separate robust priors from overfit ones.
assessments.whyNotFirst: It IS first; the runner-up R-P5 is close but is mechanical closeout with mechanism selection already complete, yielding lower marginal research value.

assessments.closureRisk: Low-to-moderate — could reveal a latent defect at final gates, but mechanism selection is already complete so closure is mostly mechanical.
assessments.dominantCost: Executing final acceptance gates and release mechanics; low intellectual cost.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable and physical gates, commit exact P5 source if gates pass, graduate through structured self-release.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Mechanism selection is complete; remaining work is exact final acceptance gates, commit, and structured self-release.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Mechanism selection is largely complete; the marginal research value of another budget unit is mostly release mechanics rather than new discovery.

assessments.closureRisk: Moderate — the research question may resolve to 'no narrower surface justified', which is a valid but lower-value closure.
assessments.dominantCost: Dependency-graph audit and packaging candidate construction; payoff is conditional on whether a narrower surface is even justified.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Audit Host import/dependency graph, build smallest packaging candidate only if measurable, dogfood against World and another non-MCP consumer.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: A narrower core/domain/extension install surface may be justified for non-MCP consumers without duplicating Host authority.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Conditional payoff: the budget may only establish that no narrower surface is justified, and semantic compatibility already passed 44 tests.

assessments.closureRisk: High — externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery; budget cannot unblock it.
assessments.dominantCost: External DNS blocker; experiments cannot run until DeepSeek DNS recovers.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Retry no-tool incremental after DNS recovery, run replay/batch and resolved-provider controls, compare utilization and decision quality.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: No-tool control-path hardening is causally admitted in source; live experiments would compare incremental/replay/batch utilization and decision quality.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Externally blocked; allocating budget now cannot advance the experiment. Deferred.

assessments.closureRisk: Very high — blocked regardless of budget; no amount of research budget closes the external host gap.
assessments.dominantCost: Dominant external admission blocker: no independent Linux/systemd host exists; budget cannot procure infrastructure.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent Linux/systemd host, verify immutable deployment kit, provision purpose-separated signers and executor-only Trade credential.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Negative control: cannot graduate to live effect without an independently administered Linux/systemd host; current WSL/Windows workstation cannot satisfy high-assurance separation.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Negative control with a dominant external admission blocker; deferred entirely.

result.choiceRationale: G-AF3 is the only candidate that is both unblocked and at a genuine decision frontier: AF002 is complete, but robustness/generalization claims are not yet earned because the fixed Genesis has almost no real environment variation. The next unit of budget directly produces materially different encounter variants and separates surviving priors from fixed-encounter overfit — a clear defect-discovery / prior-narrowing payoff with low closure risk (the work is self-contained and not externally gated). R-P5 is close behind but is largely in mechanical closeout (final gates, commit, release) with mechanism selection already complete, so marginal research value is lower. HOST-PKG is exploratory but the payoff is conditional on whether a narrower surface is even justified. H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery (defer). F-C2-BLOCKED is a negative control with a dominant external admission blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) — cannot close regardless of budget.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether G-AF3's perturbation experiments reveal that AF002 priors are fixed-encounter overfit (defect-discovery) versus genuinely topology/position/resource/target-robust (prior-generalization). This discriminates the frontier delta type and determines whether the game owner's generalization claim is earned.
result.selectionFalsifier: If the next budget were instead given to R-P5 and its final portable/physical gates unexpectedly fail, revealing a latent mechanism defect that the closeout was assumed to have resolved, then R-P5 would have had higher marginal value than G-AF3.
